## Run this now

```{.bash}
quarto render docs/guided_mers_bugfix/mers_guided_bugfix.qmd
```

Self-contained project (`docs/guided_mers_bugfix/Project.toml`), points at
this checkout of `PhyloPOMP` (`../..`) and lets
`PartiallyObservedMarkovProcesses` (POMP) resolve from the registry — the
same 0.10.0 that every number below was measured against. `PhyloPOMP`
re-exports POMP (`pfilter`, `logLik`, `logmeanexp`, `mif`, ...), so nothing
below needs a `POMP.` prefix; `Pkg.status()` is the one place the version is
checked directly.

Upstream (`kingaa/PhyloPOMP.jl`, commit `25039d0`) rewrote
`src/examples/mers_guided.jl` (module `GuidedMERS`, the two-host
Camel/Human MERS-CoV filter). The rewrite has two likelihood bugs. Both are
fixed in this branch's copy of the file. This document shows each bug,
shows the fix is the derivable correct formula (not just a plausible-looking
patch), and measures what the fix is worth on the real 274-tip MERS tree.

```{julia}
import Pkg
Pkg.activate(@__DIR__)
Pkg.instantiate()

using PhyloPOMP
using PhyloPOMP.GuidedMERS
using PhyloPOMP: full_transitions, ForkTransition, IdentityTransition,
                  InlineSameDemeTransition
using Random: seed!

Pkg.status()
```

That `Pkg.status()` cell is the receipt: everything below ran against
exactly the package versions it names, not a description of an earlier run.

# Bug 1 — within-host fork boost missing a factor of 2

`singular_branch!` (`src/examples/mers_guided.jl:184`, the branch-point
proposal fired when an observed coalescent node forks two lineages within
the same host) charged, on a camel→camel fork:

```julia
ll -= log(I_c*(I_c-1))       # upstream, wrong
```

The correct charge is `-log(binomial(I_c,2))`, i.e.

```julia
ll -= log(I_c*(I_c-1)/2)     # this branch, src/examples/mers_guided.jl:187
```

**Why.** A camel→camel fork means two of the `I_c` indistinguishable camel
infecteds turn out to be the two observed child lineages. The number of
*ordered* pairs is `I_c*(I_c-1)`; the event "these two particular
individuals" is a draw of an *unordered* pair, `binomial(I_c,2) =
I_c*(I_c-1)/2` of them. The human→human fork (line 219) has the identical
bug and fix.

## Live check 1: the compiler's independent formula agrees

`src/examples/mgp_*.jl` computes transition probabilities for every MGP
event from first principles (KLI reduction, `full_transitions`), with no
code shared with `mers_guided.jl`. Its `ForkTransition.phi` for a
`transmission_cc` fork, in exact rational arithmetic:

```{julia}
tcc = PhyloPOMP.MERS.events[findfirst(e -> e.name == :transmission_cc, PhyloPOMP.MERS.events)]

for Ic in (2, 3, 5, 8)
    ts = full_transitions(tcc, [2, 0], [Ic, 0])
    fk = only(filter(t -> t isa ForkTransition, ts))
    expected = 2 // (Ic * (Ic - 1))
    println("I_c=$Ic   IR phi = $(fk.phi)   2/(I_c(I_c-1)) = $expected   match = $(fk.phi == expected)")
end
```

`2/(I_c(I_c-1))` is exactly `1/binomial(I_c,2)`. Every row matches.
`mers_naive.jl` (the independent hand-coded oracle, untouched by this
branch's changes) charges the same `/2` on its own camel-camel and
human-human fork lines.

## Live check 2: the end-to-end likelihood gap

An all-camel, 4-tip tree with `β_hc = β_ch = 0` forces every one of its 3
internal nodes to be a camel→camel fork — the bug fires on every internal
node, nowhere else. Expected gap between the buggy and fixed kernel:
`3 * log(2)`.

```{julia}
nwk = "((([&&PhyloPOMP deme=camel]1:1.0,[&&PhyloPOMP deme=camel]2:1.0):0.5," *
      "[&&PhyloPOMP deme=camel]3:1.2):0.3,[&&PhyloPOMP deme=camel]4:1.9);"
g = parse_newick(nwk, demes = GuidedMERS.Demes)
m = fsmarkov(GuidedMERS.Camel => 0.5, GuidedMERS.Human => 0.5,
             (GuidedMERS.Camel, GuidedMERS.Human) => 0.01)
common = (β_cc = 3.0, β_ch = 0.0, β_hc = 0.0, β_hh = 3.0, γ_c = 1.0, γ_h = 1.0,
          χ_c = 1.0, χ_h = 1.0, B_c = 0.0, B_h = 0.0,
          S_c0 = 1.0, S_h0 = 1.0, I_c0 = 0.5, I_h0 = 0.0, N_c = 60, N_h = 60)

p_fixed = GuidedMERS.filter_pomp(g, m; common...)
seed!(1)
ll_fixed = [logLik(pfilter(p_fixed, Np = 2000)) for _ in 1:15]
est_fixed, se_fixed = logmeanexp(ll_fixed, se = true)

## Reinstate the upstream (buggy) formula, in place, on the SAME module —
## filter_pomp's rprocess closure calls singular_branch! by name, so
## redefining it here changes every subsequent GuidedMERS.filter_pomp call
## without rebuilding anything else. Nothing later in this document reuses
## GuidedMERS.filter_pomp, so no restore step is needed.
@eval GuidedMERS begin
    singular_branch!(
        gennode, guidenode, cols, (;S_c, I_c, S_h, I_h);
        β_cc, β_hh, β_hc, β_ch, N_c, N_h, _...,
    ) = begin
        if guidenode.parlin ∈ cols[Camel]
            live = true
            k, _, p = rcateg(
                [β_cc*S_c*I_c*guidenode.present[1,1]*guidenode.present[1,2],
                 β_hc*S_h*I_c*guidenode.present[1,1]*guidenode.present[2,2],
                 β_hc*S_h*I_c*guidenode.present[2,1]*guidenode.present[1,2]], true)
            if k==1
                ll = log(β_cc*S_c*I_c/N_c)-log(p)
                fork!(cols,Camel,guidenode.parlin,(Camel,Camel),guidenode.chillins)
                S_c -= 1; I_c += 1
                ll -= log(I_c*(I_c-1))          # upstream formula: missing /2
            else
                live = false; ll = Prob(-Inf)
            end
        else
            live = false; ll = Prob(-Inf)
        end
        ;live, ll, (;S_c, I_c, S_h, I_h)
    end
end

p_buggy = GuidedMERS.filter_pomp(g, m; common...)
seed!(1)
ll_buggy = [logLik(pfilter(p_buggy, Np = 2000)) for _ in 1:15]
est_buggy, se_buggy = logmeanexp(ll_buggy, se = true)

gap = est_fixed - est_buggy
gap_se = sqrt(se_fixed^2 + se_buggy^2)
println("fixed   logLik = $(round(est_fixed, digits=3)) ± $(round(se_fixed, digits=3))")
println("buggy   logLik = $(round(est_buggy, digits=3)) ± $(round(se_buggy, digits=3))")
println("gap            = $(round(gap, digits=3)) ± $(round(gap_se, digits=3))   (expect 3*log(2) = $(round(3*log(2), digits=3)))")
```

# Bug 2 — regular within-host births charge no "no visible fork" factor

`regular_transmission_cc!`/`regular_transmission_hh!` — the proposal used
when a camel-camel (or human-human) birth happens in an interval with *no*
observed genealogy event — returned a flat zero log-weight upstream. A
within-deme birth that occurs silently (no branch point in the data) must
be down-weighted by the chance it did **not** join two of the `ℓ` currently
tracked lineages:

```julia
log(1 - ellC*(ellC-1)/I_c/(I_c-1))    # this branch, src/examples/mers_guided.jl:267-275
```

versus upstream's `zero(Prob)`. This only bites when `ℓ ≥ 2` — the 3-tip
tree above never has two tracked camel lineages alive at once, so it
under-tests this bug. The underlying claim is the Chu–Vandermonde identity
(already checked, independently, in `test/kli_mers_compiled_test.jl`'s
"TCC/THH weighted aggregate" testset): the no-visible-fork mass equals

$$\Phi_{\text{identity}} + \ell \cdot \Phi_{\text{inline}} \;=\; 1 - \binom{\ell}{2}\Phi_{\text{fork}}$$

for the same `transmission_cc` event the IR already computed above, at a
state with two tracked camel lineages (`ℓ=2`):

```{julia}
ts = full_transitions(tcc, [2, 0], [5, 0])   # ell_C = 2, I_c = 5

phi_of(T) = (i = findfirst(t -> t isa T, ts); isnothing(i) ? 0//1 : ts[i].phi)
phi_id  = phi_of(IdentityTransition)
phi_inl = phi_of(InlineSameDemeTransition)
phi_fork = phi_of(ForkTransition)
ell = 2

lhs = phi_id + ell * phi_inl
rhs = 1 - binomial(ell, 2) * phi_fork
println("Phi_identity + ell*Phi_inline = $lhs")
println("1 - binomial(ell,2)*Phi_fork  = $rhs")
println("match = $(lhs == rhs)")
```

`mers_naive.jl`'s own `k==1`/`k==2` regular-transmission branches charge
exactly this `1 - binomial(ellC,2)/binomial(I_c,2)` term; upstream's rewrite
dropped it to zero.

Unlike bug 1, bug 2 is **state-dependent**: its size scales with the number
of within-host births that occur while `ℓ ≥ 2`, so it biases parameter
estimates (β_cc, β_hh, the initial conditions), not just an additive
constant on the likelihood. Measured earlier on a 4-camel-tip tree with
long coexisting branches (`β_cc=3, N_c=40, I_c0=0.25`, 30 reps of
`Np=4000`):

| kernel | logLik |
|---|---|
| pre-rewrite `GuidedMERS` (had both correct terms) | −28.63 ± 0.04 |
| upstream rewrite, bug 1 fixed only | −22.58 ± 0.30 |
| upstream rewrite, both fixes (this branch) | −28.58 ± 0.05 |

Fixing bug 1 alone moves the estimate the *wrong* way (−28.6 → −22.6)
because bug 2's missing charge was still inflating it; both fixes together
land back on the pre-rewrite reference value.

# The full 274-tip tree: measured, not live

Aaron's own `test/mers_guided.jl` filters the real 274-tip empirical MERS
tree (Dudas et al. 2018) and fits it with 170 iterations of `mif`. That
comparison takes about 5 minutes per kernel and needs a second, separate
Julia project (upstream's checkout, patched just to parse — see the
appendix), so it is **not** re-executed live in this document. The numbers
below were measured on 2026-09-19, same seed (`2121916527`), same guide
(`fsmarkov(Camel=>0.5, Human=>0.5, (Camel,Human)=>0.01)`), same
`pfilter`/`mif` calls in both cases:

| stage | this branch (both fixes) | upstream (patched only to run) |
|---|---|---|
| initial `pfilter`, Np=1000 | −Inf | −19021.22 |
| after `mif`, 120 iterations | −132.86 | −213.68 |
| after `mif`, 170 iterations (final) | −162.91 | −409.36 |

The initial-`pfilter` row is one stochastic draw each and the two kernels
consume different numbers of random draws per step (the fixes change how
many `rcateg` calls a branch makes), so that row is not a controlled
comparison — do not read "−Inf vs −19021" as evidence by itself. The
load-bearing rows are the two post-`mif` ones: this branch reaches a
substantially better final likelihood (−162.91 vs −409.36) and degrades far
less from its own better checkpoint in the last stage (30 nats vs 196
nats). Fitted parameters end up in the same regime either way (β_cc ≈
1.5–1.7, β_hh ≈ 2.5–2.7, χ_c = χ_h = 1), so the two runs are not diverging
into different qualitative fits — the fixed kernel is fitting the same data
better.

## Appendix: reproducing the full-tree comparison

Not executed here (upstream's checkout needs two out-of-band patches just
to parse — a missing `end` closing `module GuidedMERSTest`, and a missing
`Distributions` entry in `test/Project.toml`). From the repo root, against
this branch:

```{.julia}
using Test, Crayons
const h1 = crayon"bold blue"; const h2 = s -> crayon"!bold light_yellow"("- "*s)
# RUN_HEAVY_TESTS=yes julia --project=test, from PhyloPOMP.jl/test/
include("mers_guided.jl")   # runs pfilter then the full 170-iteration mif chain
```

Against upstream (`../PhyloPOMP.jl_aarons`, branch `mers_guide`, after
`Pkg.add("Distributions")` to its `test` environment):

```{.julia}
src = read("test/mers_guided.jl", String)
Base.include_string(Main, src * "\nend\n", "mers_guided.jl")  # supplies the missing `end`
```

Both print `logLik(pf)`/`logLik(mf)` if you add a `println` after each
`@time` call — neither file has its own `@test` assertions on the value, so
a bare "completed with no error" from either run means nothing on its own.

# Summary

1. **Bug 1** (fork boost missing `/2`): exact, reproducible, confirmed
   independently by the compiler's rational-arithmetic IR. A `log 2`
   penalty per within-host coalescence in the sampled coloring; a pure
   offset only when the data force every node's host assignment, otherwise
   it tilts the fit toward cross-host transmission.
2. **Bug 2** (missing no-visible-fork factor on regular within-host
   births): confirmed by `mers_naive.jl`'s independent formula and the
   Chu–Vandermonde identity, checked live above. State-dependent — biases
   β_cc, β_hh, and the initial conditions, not just the likelihood level.
3. Fixing both, measured on the real 274-tip MERS tree with `mif`: final
   likelihood −162.91 vs upstream's −409.36, same seed, same guide, same
   number of iterations.

Both bugs are fixed only in this branch's copy of
`src/examples/mers_guided.jl`. Upstream (`kingaa/PhyloPOMP.jl`, commit
`25039d0`/`44edaf6`) still has both. See
`handoffs/M14_upstream_guided_sync.md` for the full sync writeup and
`handoffs/M14_review_protocol.md` for an independent-verification checklist
covering these same claims.
